div.head: Norðleoda 3
div.ab: Episcopi et aldermanni octo milia þrimsa.
Bisceopes and ealdermannes, VIII þusend þrymsa.
eines Bischofs und Ealdorman 8000 Tremissen [100 Pfund],
of a bishop and an ealdorman 8,000 thrymsas [100 pounds],
That of a bishop and an ealdorman 8,000 thrymsas.
For a bishop and an ealdorman, eight thousand thrymsas.
div.note: and ‘ðrymsa’ corrected to H's ‘þrymsa’. Liebermann compares the Instituta Cnuti III 57: ‘Episcopus et comes habent … leges equales’.

ealdorman: A royal appointee charged with overseeing portions of the kingdom. Within the political hierarchy of early eleventhcentury England, ealdormen were considered of higher rank than a reeve but below that of members of the royal family. The ealdorman’s responsibilities included presiding over courts, levying taxes, and supplying soldiers at the king’s request.
